prerequisites: Participation certificate for a standardisation test for the Bachelor of Engineering Science and Bachelor of Engineering Science: Architecture programs

learning_outcomes.text: The student is familiar with and understands the basic principles of proof and logical reasoning.
The student is familiar with the basic properties of real and complex numbers.

The student knows the definitions and basic properties of functions of real numbers and functions of vectors. The student is able to work fluently with elementary functions (e.g., trigonometric, inverse trigonometric, hyperbolic, exponential, logarithmic, etc.).

The student recognizes different coordinate systems in both two- and three-dimensional space, can switch between these systems, and is able to make an informed choice when solving a problem (e.g., integration). The covered coordinate systems are polar, cylindrical, and spherical coordinates.
The student can represent curves in both two- and three-dimensional space as well as surfaces in various ways, namely explicitly, implicitly, and parametrically.

Students know the basic principles of analysis (Riemann integration, differentiation, directional derivatives, chain rule) and are able to apply them to concrete (engineering) problems such as determining the volume and surface area of a surface of revolution, the length of a curve, calculating the center of mass, and the moment of inertia.

The student can apply the local approximation theorems of differential calculus, both directly and implicitly, to calculate tangents and tangent surfaces. They can relate the concepts of gradient, Jacobian, etc., to this.

syllabus_topics: Chapter 2: Basic concepts of analytical geometry
Cauchy sequence, completeness of real numbers
Limit and continuity for functions of several variables
Chapter 5: Derivatives of functions of 1 variable
Exercises on: Chapter 1: Numbers, vectors, and functions
Exercises on: Chapter 2: Basic concepts of analytical geometry
Exercises on: Chapter 4: Limits and continuity
Exercises on: Chapter 5: Derivatives of functions of 1 variable
Exercises on: Chapter 6: Derivatives of multivariate functions
assessment_rules: A midterm test is organized. If the student passes the midterm test and achieves a better result on it than on the exam during the next examination period, the midterm test result will be included in the final result for that period, weighted at one-fourth for the midterm and three-fourths for the exam. This recalculation does not apply to results obtained in the third examination period (resit). The exam is open book; textbooks, slides, exercise bundles, and self-written notes are allowed, as is a simple calculator meeting faculty criteria. For resits, there is no recalculation of midterm test scores.
